title: Start a short PCSX2 test in turbo mode

Start a short PCSX2 test in turbo mode

blocks.text: PCSX2 lists `-turbo` as entering turbo (fast-forward) mode after startup. This is useful for a short wait or repeatable test where accelerated emulation is intended. It is a speed mode, not a performance fix: it can make audio, input timing, and frame pacing unsuitable for judging normal gameplay.

Use a title or homebrew that you can safely exit and whose current save is backed up. Identify the emulator’s turbo hotkey before launching. Do not compare frame rate, audio latency, controller responsiveness, or thermals while the launch begins in fast-forward; those measurements require normal-speed conditions.

items: 1. Copy the known-good PCSX2 launcher and keep the original unchanged.
2. Add `-turbo` before the game image argument.
3. Boot a safe menu or short test and verify the interface indicates accelerated emulation by its behavior.
4. Use the known turbo hotkey to return to normal speed before entering a timing-sensitive section.
5. Check that audio and input behave normally after leaving turbo.
6. Close the title normally and launch again without the option for ordinary play.

blocks.text: Pass when the copied launch begins in the expected fast-forward state and the turbo toggle returns emulation to normal speed. Compare the same menu at normal speed before drawing any conclusion about performance or compatibility. An apparent speed increase under turbo says nothing about whether the device can sustain normal full-speed emulation.

items: No obvious turbo indicator: confirm the option is before the boot filename and test with a known hotkey.
Audio sounds wrong: return to normal speed; turbo is expected to alter timing.
Performance seems better: rerun without turbo before measuring frame pacing.
The save state or menu behaves unexpectedly: close normally and restore the pre-test backup if data changed.

blocks.text: Remove `-turbo` from the copied command and launch normally. If the hotkey did not exit turbo, close the game through PCSX2’s regular menu and restart without the option. Do not use a fast-forward session to save progress in a timing-sensitive game.
